name: Ganga
description: The holiest river in Hinduism, flowing from the Gangotri Glacier in the Himalayas to the Bay of Bengal. Spans 2,525 km across the northern Indian subcontinent.
historicalSignificance: Considered the mother goddess Ganga, purveyor of moksha (salvation). Cities like Varanasi, Allahabad, and Haridwar are sacred pilgrimage sites along its banks.

name: Yamuna
description: The largest tributary of the Ganga, flowing parallel to the Ganga for 1,376 km. Arises from the Yamunotri Glacier in the Himalayas.
historicalSignificance: Considered the daughter of the sun god Surya and the goddess Yamuna. The Yamuna-Ganga sangam at Prayagraj is a major pilgrimage site.

name: Saraswati
description: The sacred river described in the Vedas as a flowing river of light. Now believed to be the Ghaggar-Hakra river that dried up around 2600 BCE.
historicalSignificance: Mentioned extensively in the Rig Veda as a divine river flowing from the mountains to the sea. The Indus Valley civilization flourished along its banks.

name: Narmada
description: The fifth longest river in the Indian subcontinent at 1,312 km, flowing from the Amarkantak Plateau to the Arabian Sea. One of the seven sacred rivers in Hinduism.
historicalSignificance: Called the Rewa in ancient texts. The Narmada Parikrama pilgrimage circuit is one of the longest walking pilgrimages at over 2,600 km.

name: Brahmaputra
description: One of the major rivers of Asia, originating in the Tibetan Himalayas and flowing through India and Bangladesh for 3,969 km to the Bay of Bengal.
historicalSignificance: Known as the son of Brahma, it is unique among major rivers as it is masculine in gender in Hindu tradition. The Majuli island in Assam is the largest river island.

name: Kaveri
description: A sacred river of South India, flowing from the Talacauvery Hills in Karnataka to the Bay of Bengal in Tamil Nadu. Spans 802 km through the Deccan Plateau.
historicalSignificance: Known as the Ganga of the South, it is considered a divine river in Tamil Nadu. The Kumbakonam temples and the Rameshwaram pilgrimage routes follow its course.

name: Godavari
description: The second longest river in India after the Ganga, flowing 1,465 km from the Western Ghats near Nashik to the Bay of Bengal in Andhra Pradesh.
historicalSignificance: Known as Dakshina Ganga (Ganga of the South). The Kumbh Mela at Nashik is held on its banks. The river is mentioned in the Ramayana as flowing through the Dandaka forest.

name: Krishna
description: The fourth longest river in India at 1,400 km, originating near Mahabaleshwar in the Western Ghats and flowing eastward to the Bay of Bengal.
historicalSignificance: Named after Lord Krishna. The river basin was home to the Satavahana, Chalukya, and Vijayanagara empires. Srisailam and Nagarjunasagar dams are built across it.

name: Sindhu
description: The Indus River — one of the longest rivers in Asia at 3,180 km. It originates near Mount Kailash in Tibet and flows through Kashmir and Pakistan to the Arabian Sea.
historicalSignificance: The river that gave India its name. The Indus Valley Civilization (Harappa, Mohenjo-daro) flourished along its banks from 3300 BCE. Mentioned as Sindhu in the Vedas.

name: Gandaki
description: Also known as Narayani, the Gandaki originates in the Himalayas of Nepal and flows south to join the Ganga near Patna in Bihar. It is 630 km long.
historicalSignificance: Sacred in both Hinduism and Buddhism. The shaligrama stones found in the Gandaki riverbed are worshipped as forms of Lord Vishnu. The river is mentioned in the Mahabharata.

name: Mahanadi
description: A major east-flowing river of central India, the Mahanadi spans 858 km from the highlands of Chhattisgarh to the Bay of Bengal in Odisha. It forms one of the largest deltas in India.
historicalSignificance: Mentioned in ancient texts as the great river of Kalinga. The Hirakud Dam, one of the longest dams in the world, is built across it. The river basin supported the ancient Kalinga civilization.
